## Goal

As a producer, I want test-generated artefacts to stay out of the working tree, so that the dev-push full-suite gate is never discarded as `state_changed_during_run` simply because a browser test produced an attachment.

## Problem

`implement.py finish` runs the full suite in the item's worktree and discards the verdict when the checkout's `git status --porcelain=v1 -uall` surface changes mid-run (`snapshot_own_checkout` / `state_changed_during_run`, SA-0MW3FF18I003KGZE). Vitest 4's browser projects write `context.annotate` attachments to `<root>/.vitest-attachments/` (default `attachmentsDir`). That directory is **not** in `.gitignore`, so any run that produces an attachment (observed: the same 102 KB PNG, deterministic across two runs) leaves an untracked path behind, the fingerprint differs before/after, and the gate reports `full_suite_red` / `reason: infrastructure` — nothing is committed or pushed and the item is released to `open`.

Observed on this checkout during `CG-0MWNSR376002QBY9` (two consecutive finishes, same hash). Workaround used locally: added `.vitest-attachments/` to `.git/info/exclude` (local, untracked).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.vitest-attachments/` (and any other root-level Vitest attachment output) is ignored repo-wide, either by adding it to `.gitignore` or by pinning `attachmentsDir` outside the repo in `vite.config.ts`.
- A full-suite run that produces an attachment leaves `git status --porcelain` unchanged, so `implement.py finish` is not discarded as `state_changed_during_run`.
- The chosen fix is recorded in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (testing section) if it changes the developer workflow.

## Notes

`discovered-from:CG-0MWNSR376002QBY9`. Low risk, XS effort. The local `.git/info/exclude` workaround is not shared with other clones or CI, so this item exists to fix it at the repo level.


## Impact

A browser test that writes a Vitest attachment no longer silently discards a green full-suite verdict, so a finished change reaches `dev` instead of failing as an unexplained infrastructure red.

Run the human browser playtest the GDD recommends (ideally three people, at least one who has not read the content) over the v1 Long Erasure content, and record measured wall-clock run durations, phone-screen readability and felt tension.

## Why

The v1 scope statement (CG-0MWPY2HJU006LJMU, GDD §7.2) estimates playtime at 13 minutes a run (10–16 range) from the measured beats-per-run figure (spike: 6–10 beats, mean 8.48) multiplied by two stated, unmeasured assumptions: 35–50 s a beat (A1) and ~3 min presentation overhead (A2). This playtest is the measurement that replaces A1 and A2. It also closes the evidence limit recorded in GDD §2.6 (agent-driven structural measurement, not felt enjoyment) and lifts deferral D3 of the GDD's deferred list (§7.6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Three participants (at least one who has not read the content) each play at least one complete run in a browser, with wall-clock duration recorded from opening to epilogue.
- The measured durations are compared with the 10–16 minute range and the 13-minute target; the difference and its cause are recorded.
- Phone-screen readability (or a named proxy viewport) is assessed and any blocking issue is filed as its own work item.
- Findings are recorded in docs/design/storyline-playtest-evaluation.md and the playtime basis in GDD §7.2 is updated or confirmed.

## Impact

A producer can replace the v1 playtime estimate's two unmeasured assumptions with measured human run durations.

## Goal

As a content author, I want the Gym story-line demo to play the authored
`example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv` at runtime, so that an edit made in
`npm run storylines:editor` is visible in the Gym scene without hand-editing a
second copy in TypeScript.

## Impact

A content author can now edit the Gym story-line in the story-line editor and
reload the demo to see their own card names, prose, option costs and state
gates play exactly as authored — with no TypeScript edit and no second card
catalogue to keep in step.

## Problem

`GymStorylineScene` renders `DEMO_CARDS`, a hard-coded catalogue in
`example-games/gym/GymStorylineDemo.ts`. Nothing in the scene's runtime path
reads the CSV (`createSceneRuntime()` -> `createDemoRuntime()` -> `DEMO_CARDS`;
no `fetch`, no `?raw` import, no CSV parse). Consequences:

- Editor edits to `storylines.csv` never reach the Gym scene — observed
  2026-11-22: the author renamed `gym-story-start` to "Town Roads", rewrote its
  `context` and `effect`, regenerated the manifest/Mermaid, restarted the dev
  server, and saw no change in the demo.
- The catalogue and the CSV are kept in sync only by a test assertion
  (`tests/gym/GymStorylineContent.test.ts` -> "carries the same card ids,
  context and authored outcomes as the CSV"), so a content edit leaves the
  suite red until a developer copies the prose across by hand.
- The two copies have already diverged mechanically: the CSV's `Invest` option
  carries `#cost=coins:5#extra=reputation:+2#when=coins>=100>gym-story-end`,
  while `DEMO_CARDS` carries only `#says`. The parity test does not compare
  option mechanics, so the played demo is not mechanically the authored
  content.

`GymLongErasureGame.ts` is the existing in-repo precedent for the desired
shape: it imports its CSV via `?raw` and builds content with
`longErasureContentFromCsv()` (`src/story-line/content/csv.ts`).

## Approach (suggested, not prescriptive)

1. Load `storylines.csv` into `GymStorylineDemo` — either a `?raw` import in
   the Gym layer (mirroring Long Erasure) or a shared helper that parses via
   `cardsFromCsv(parseCsv(text), GYM_CONTENT_ADAPTER)`.
2. Derive the demo's card catalogue from the parsed content instead of the
   literal `DEMO_CARDS` array, keeping the demo's `DemoCard` view shape
   (including `context` and `#says` -> `StorylineOption.says`).
3. Decide and document the fate of the frozen-mechanics baseline
   (`tests/fixtures/story-line/prose/gym-storyline-mechanics-baseline.json`)
   once the CSV is the single source: either keep it as a content-change guard
   fed from the CSV, or replace it with a checksum/parity assertion.
4. Keep the `setGymStorylineDemoRuntimeFactory()` test seam working (the
   browser "context absent" layout test depends on injecting an alternate

## Goal

As a developer, I want a stale/dangling composed-asset symlink to never break a build, so a Vite build (and the tests that run one) succeeds in any checkout — including audit execution worktrees under `.worklog/worktrees/` — instead of failing with `ENOENT` on a missing game asset.

## Context

Discovered while auditing `CG-0MWSJ8RJM001IRCJ` (Gym story-line "Public Investment" cost change). The audit's full-suite execution in `.worklog/worktrees/audit-exec-CG-0MWSJ8RJM001IRCJ` went RED with two failures in `tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts`:

```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat '.../audit-exec-CG-0MWSJ8RJM001IRCJ/public/assets/cards/lost-cities/lc-red-inv3-sm.svg'
  ❯ copyDir node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-D4NMHUTW.js
  ❯ buildToTemp tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts:31
```

Root cause:

- `scripts/vite-game-assets-plugin.ts:10-16` runs `composeGameAssets` in `configResolved` so Vite's public-dir scan/copy sees composed sibling-game asset symlinks.
- `scripts/link-game-assets.ts:198-208` creates those links with **relative** targets derived from the launcher repo root (`path.relative(path.dirname(dest), source)`). Inside `.worklog/worktrees/<id>/` the same relative target resolves one directory too shallow (`<repo>/.worklog/worktrees/tce-lost-cities/…`, which has no `public/` tree), so the link **dangles**.
- `public/assets/cards/lost-cities` is not in the managed asset contract (`scripts/configs/repo-layout.json:95` core `assets` list), so a `GAMES_CONFIG=core-only` composition never prunes/repairs it, and Vite's public-dir copy then aborts.

Impact: two later clean executions at the same commit (`7e0bf526`) were GREEN, so the failure is composition-state dependent rather than a dev-HEAD regression — but any checkout carrying a stale link (worktree, switched preset, removed sibling) fails `npm run build`, and audits intermittently triage phantom critical `test-failure` items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A composed-asset destination that resolves to a non-existent source (dangling link) can never fail a build: either `composeGameAssets` prunes links it owns that are dangling, or every sibling-owned card/asset root (`cards/lost-cities` today, others in `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json`) is covered by the managed asset contract so a preset change removes it.
- A regression test proves the fix: a worktree-style layout (`<repo>/.worklog/worktrees/<id>/public/assets/…`) containing a dangling composed link still builds, or `composeGameAssets` removes it (extend `tests/scripts/link-game-assets.test.ts`).
- `tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts` passes in an isolated worktree that also carries composed asset links (the case that failed at `7e0bf526`).
- `npm run build` and the unit suite are green from a fresh worktree.

## Impact

Builds and test runs stop failing on stale composed-asset links, so working in a worktree or after switching game presets no longer needs manual symlink clean-up.

## Related Work

- `CG-0MWSJ8RJM001IRCJ` — discovered-from (audit of the Gym story-line cost change; unrelated to that item's work)
- `CG-0MWTOUXMY004F5N8` — the triage `test-failure` item for this failure, waived as an audit-execution environment artefact and re-parented here to carry the provenance

# Make game-asset and game-source sibling resolution worktree-aware

## Problem

When a build runs from a worktree directory (`.worklog/worktrees/<id>/`), sibling game path resolution (e.g. `../tce-main-street` from `configs/full.json`) resolves relative to the worktree root instead of the main checkout. This causes `planGameAssetLinks` (link-game-assets.ts) and `discoverGames` (vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts) to look at `.worklog/worktrees/tce-<game>` — another item's checkout or nothing — instead of the canonical `<main-checkout>/../tce-<game>`.

## Users

- Developer running `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run build` from a worktree.
- Audit/CI runs that invoke build from worktrees.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `planGameAssetLinks` (link-game-assets.ts) and `discoverGames` (vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts) resolve sibling paths relative to the main checkout when `projectRoot` is inside `.worklog/worktrees/<id>/`, using `<main-checkout>/../tce-<game>` instead of `<worktree>/../tce-<game>`.
- Non-worktree builds (running from the main checkout) behave identically to today.
- A unit test pins the worktree-inside sibling resolution case in `tests/scripts/link-game-assets.test.ts` or `tests/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.test.ts`.
- `npm run build` and the unit suite stay green.

## Impact

A developer running a full-preset build from a worktree sees the correct game assets instead of silently picking up another item's checkout or missing assets entirely.

## Constraints

- The fix must not affect non-worktree builds (the common case).
- The fix must not change the composition/pruning logic in link-game-assets.ts — only the path resolution anchor.

## Existing state

- `vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`: `discoverGames()` resolves `entry.path` via `path.resolve(projectRoot, entry.path)`.
- `link-game-assets.ts`: `planGameAssetLinks()` resolves game paths via `path.resolve(options.projectRoot, game.path)`.
- `vite-game-assets-plugin.ts`: passes `projectRoot` from Vite's config root (which is the worktree dir when run from inside `.worklog/worktrees/<id>/`).
- Dangling link pruning (CG-0MWTSRRWU0062OMI) already handles the *symptom* (prunes stale links) but not the *root cause* (wrong resolution anchor).
- `tests/scripts/link-game-assets.test.ts` has a worktree-style layout test but uses `tce-golf` as a sibling path (not the canonical `../tce-golf`).

## Key Files

- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — `discoverGames()` resolves sibling paths; needs worktree-aware anchor.
- `scripts/link-game-assets.ts` — `planGameAssetLinks()` resolves sibling paths; needs worktree-aware anchor.
- `vite.config.ts` — passes `__dirname` to plugins (main checkout anchor); may need to detect worktree context.
- `tests/scripts/link-game-assets.test.ts` — add worktree-inside sibling resolution test.

## Related Work

- `CG-0MWTSRRWU0062OMI` — Composed-asset symlink composition is worktree-fragile (dangling link fails vite build). Fixes the build failure symptom; this item addresses the resolution root cause.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope:** Both asset resolution (`planGameAssetLinks`) and game-source resolution (`discoverGames`) share the same sibling-path resolution pattern and must be fixed together.
- **Assumption:** A worktree directory is identifiable by walking up from `projectRoot` to find the first parent that contains both `.worklog/` and `configs/` (i.e. the main checkout).
- **Risk:** A distribution checkout that happens to have a `.worklog/` directory at an unexpected level could be misdetected. Mitigation: require the main-checkout ancestor to also have `configs/<preset>.json` for the active preset.
- **Risk:** Existing tests (e.g. the worktree-style layout test in `link-game-assets.test.ts`) use `tce-golf` as a sibling path, not `../tce-golf`; the new test must use the canonical sibling path to be meaningful.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions — the existing description and repo context are sufficient.

## Summary

Add the scene-space enumeration core: a pure, Phaser-free module that walks the runtime's own
scene/beat/close/routing transitions over the **manifest + its content**, recording every scene
exit and every beat refusal inside the existing depth/state bounds.

This is the engine seam both invariants read; it must reproduce the runtime's decisions, not a
second copy of them.

## Context

- The parent's "Proposed shape" fixes the state tuple: `(scene, beat, clock remaining, resources,
  outcome rules applied)`, enumerated with the existing `maxDepth` / `maxStates` bounds, a bound
  hit staying a failure.
- `src/story-line/content/guard.ts` already carries the bounded-DFS, state-key and truncation
  reporting machinery to mirror; `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` already exports the pure
  decision helpers the runtime uses (`evaluateSceneCondition`, `classifySceneOutcome`,
  `selectRoute`, `resolveRouteTarget`).
- The clock is **not** a declared resource, which is exactly why this enumeration needs its own
  module: the CSV guard cannot see it.

## Scope

**In:** the enumeration model, its state key and bound handling, its report shape (explored
states, scene exits, refusals, truncation), and a parity test against the real runner.

**Out:** the two invariants (their own children), the CLI mode, documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/story-line/content/scene-guard.ts` exports `enumerateSceneSpace(manifest, cards, options)`
  returning a frozen report with: every explored state key, every observed scene exit (scene id,
  winning outcome rule id, outcome, clock remaining at close, whether the close was refusal-
  triggered) and every observed beat refusal (scene id, beat card id, clock cost, clock remaining).
- Transition decisions delegate to the runtime's pure helpers — outcome and route precedence are
  never re-derived: `evaluateSceneCondition`, `classifySceneOutcome`, `selectRoute`,
  `resolveRouteTarget` from `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts`, and `isOptionAffordable` from
  `src/story-line/compile.ts`.
- A parity test drives a real `createEpisodeRunner` over the clean control fixture (headless
  adapter double) along its authored routes and asserts the enumeration records the **same** scene
  exits (scene, rule id, outcome, refusal flag) for those routes.
- Bounds: `maxDepth` (beats per route) and `maxStates` (explored states) default to the CSV guard's
  values; a bound hit is reported as truncation and makes the report invalid — never a silent pass.
- Determinism: two enumerations of the same inputs produce byte-identical JSON (no clock, RNG or
  ambient state is read; state-key ordering and the JSON key order are fixed).
- Resource arithmetic mirrors today's engine exactly (unclamped, unbounded `applyResourceDelta`);
  the module comment records that the G4 clamping work (`CG-0MWR0BGVG004UE7X`) is what will later
  change the arithmetic, and a unit test pins the current unclamped behaviour.

## Minimal implementation

- Model the content once (`cardsById`, compiled options, declared keys, start bag, bounds) and
  reuse it for every branch of the DFS, as `guard.ts` does.
- Represent a state by `(sceneId, beatId, clockRemaining, pendingChain, resource bag)`; apply an
  option's cost/extra effect with the same ordering the choice model uses and stop at an ending.
- Record refusals at the entry step (cost > remaining) as the close trigger and continue into the
  close + routing step, so the refusal's continuation is part of the same enumeration.
- Emit `sceneGuardToJson(report)` and `formatSceneGuardReport(report)` beside the existing guard
  serialisers, in the same style.

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/content/scene-guard.ts` (new)
- `src/story-line/content/guard.ts` (read/pattern reference — bounds, state key, reporting)
- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` (pure helpers: `evaluateSceneCondition`,
  `classifySceneOutcome`, `selectRoute`, `resolveRouteTarget`)
- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` / `src/story-line/types.ts` (`EpisodeManifest`, `Scene`,
  `Beat`, `SceneOutcome`)
- `src/story-line/compile.ts` (`isOptionAffordable`, option model)
- `tests/story-line/content/scene-guard.test.ts` (new)
- `tests/story-line/content/scene-guard-fixtures.ts` (the lane from the previous child)

## Dependencies

Depends on the test-lane child (fixtures + helper).

## Deliverables

The enumeration module, its JSON/format serialisers, and a unit suite including the runner parity
proof, bound/truncation proof, determinism proof and unclamped-arithmetic pin.

## Impact

A story author can now see every scene exit and refused beat an episode can produce — including the outcome a refused close classifies — before a player ever meets them.

## Summary

Assert the parent's first invariant — **no exhausted close classifies as `success`** — over the
enumerated scene space, and report a violation per offending scene exit.

A scene that runs out of clock is a failure by design (GDD §2.10 T3); content that silently
labels it a success truncates the player's run without telling them.

## Context

- The clock is not a declared resource, so the CSV guard cannot see this at all; only the
  scene-space enumeration (previous child) carries `budgetExhausted` into the outcome rules.
- `classifySceneOutcome` already exposes the winning `ruleId`, which makes the report precise:
  the violation names the rule that mislabelled the close, not just the scene.

## Scope

**In:** the invariant predicate, its violation record and report entry, and its tests.

**Out:** the refusal-stranding invariant (its own child), CLI exposure, documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `enumerateSceneSpace` (or a companion `evaluateSceneSpaceGuard`) reports an invariant named
  `no-success-on-exhausted-close`, with `checked` and `violations` counts in the same shape the
  CSV guard's `gated-branch-survivable` uses.
- A scene exit whose close was refusal-triggered and whose winning rule classified `success`
  produces exactly one violation naming: scene id, refused beat card id, winning `ruleId`, and the
  classified outcome.
- The `exhausted-success` control fixture fails this invariant and **only** this invariant, with
  the violation naming the fixture's recorded scene id and rule id (no incidental second
  violation).
- False-positive controls: an exhausted close that classifies `partial` or `failure` is not
  flagged, and a scene with no refusal contributes no violations.
- The `clean` control fixture passes, and a scene whose `success` close follows a **paid** beat
  (not a refusal) is not flagged.

## Minimal implementation

- Derive the predicate from the enumeration's scene-exit records (the refusal flag is already on
  the record), so no second traversal is added.
- Add the violation record to the report's `violations` array in the existing guard JSON shape.
- Tests are table-driven over the control fixtures plus an inline minimal manifest for the
  false-positive cases.

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/content/scene-guard.ts` (the invariant predicate + violation record)
- `src/story-line/content/guard.ts` (read only — `ContentGuardInvariant` / violation shape)
- `tests/story-line/content/scene-guard.test.ts` (extend)
- `tests/story-line/content/scene-guard-fixtures.ts` (control fixtures + intended-violation data)

## Dependencies

Depends on the enumeration child.

## Deliverables

The invariant, its violation reporting, the passing/failing fixture assertions, and the

## Summary

Assert the parent's second invariant — **no refusal leads to a state with no reachable ending** —
so a refused beat can never strand the player in a dead scene.

This is GDD §2.8.6 item 5 and §2.10 T3: the refusal is a failure *with* authored recovery content,
never a silent truncation.

## Context

- The refusal closes the scene (`budgetExhausted`), and the close routes through the authored
  route table; a route may loop, terminate in a non-ending beat, or reach an ending.
- The check needs its own bounded search from each refusal state; the enumeration's explored
  states and the existing bounds are the machinery to reuse.

## Scope

**In:** the reachability predicate from a refusal state to a declared ending, its violation record
and report entry, and its tests.

**Out:** the exhausted-success invariant, CLI exposure, documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The guard reports an invariant named `refusal-reaches-ending` with `checked` and `violations`
  counts, in the existing report shape.
- A refusal from which no continuation reaches any `manifest.endings` entry produces exactly one
  violation naming the scene id, the refused beat card id, the route taken on the exhausted close,
  and the terminal states the search reached instead of an ending.
- The `refusal-strand` control fixture fails this invariant and only this invariant, naming the
  fixture's recorded scene and refused beat.
- Recovery controls pass: a refusal whose exhausted-close route reaches a failure scene and then an
  ending (the GDD's `le-iii-approach` shape) is not flagged.
- A bound hit during the reachability search is reported as truncation and fails closed (never a
  pass); cycles that revisit a state terminate through the state key, so a reset ending is an
  ordinary passing shape.

## Minimal implementation

- Start the search from the exhausted close's selected route resolution (reusing
  `selectRoute` / `resolveRouteTarget`), then reuse the enumeration's successor expansion and
  state key.
- Share the bound accounting with the enumeration (one truncation report), so two invariants can
  never disagree about whether the space was fully explored.
- Tests are table-driven over the control fixtures plus an inline loop fixture.

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/content/scene-guard.ts` (reachability predicate + violation record)
- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` (read only — `selectRoute`, `resolveRouteTarget`)
- `tests/story-line/content/scene-guard.test.ts` (extend)
- `tests/story-line/content/scene-guard-fixtures.ts` (control fixtures + intended-violation data)

## Dependencies

Depends on the enumeration child. Independent of the exhausted-success invariant.

## Deliverables

The invariant, its violation reporting, the failing fixture assertion, the recovery control and the
loop/truncation proofs.

## Impact

A refused beat can no longer silently strand a run: the scene-space guard now names the scene, the refused beat, the outcome rule and the exact route a dead-end refusal took, so a writer can see and fix the missing door instead of a player reaching a dead scene with no ending.

## Summary

`tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts` intermittently fails inside the unit
suite with an `ENOENT` while Vite copies the repo's `public/` directory. The
failing path is a *composed* game-asset symlink
(`<root>/public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/upg-orchard.svg`), i.e. a link
owned by `scripts/vite-game-assets-plugin.ts` / `scripts/link-game-assets.ts`.

## Problem statement

Several unit tests build the **real** project root (real `vite.config.ts`,
real `public/`), so `gameAssetsPlugin` composes/prunes/removes symlinks in the
shared `public/assets/games` tree while another Vitest worker is walking that
same tree in Vite's `prepareOutDir → copyDir`. `copyDir` does
`readdirSync(dir)` then `statSync(entry)`; a link removed between those two
calls aborts the build with `ENOENT`. The race is preset-dependent (one worker
composes `GAMES_CONFIG=core-only` and *removes* `games/main-street`, another
composes the ambient preset — `full` under `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — and
*creates* it), so it only fires when two such builds overlap. The test then
fails for a reason unrelated to the contract it asserts (base-path/icon URLs).

## Users

- **Agent running the unit gate** (`/skill:test --type unit`, `implement.py finish` changed-scope gate). Story: as an agent, I want a red unit run to mean my change is broken, so I do not spend a cycle re-running and hunting a flake I did not cause.
- **Producer triaging a red gate / audit F3 cache miss.** Story: as a producer, I want the unit stage verdict to be reproducible, so a waiver is never needed for a race.
- **Release engineer.** Story: as a releaser, I want the full suite to be trustworthy at the commit I promote to `main`.
- **Developer running `npm test` locally** while a `npm run dev` (full preset) session is open. Story: as a developer, my test run should not be corrupted by another process composing assets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit-suite (and other automated) builds of the real project root never mutate `public/assets` — a `build()`/`createServer()` run leaves the composed-link set unchanged, pinned by a deterministic test that asserts before/after link-set equality for a real-root build (this is the reproduction: it fails on today's behaviour, where a `core-only` build removes `games/main-street`).
- `gameAssetsPlugin` keeps its current behaviour (compose / prune-dangling / remove-stale) for every non-test invocation (`npm run dev`, `npm run build`, `build:electron`, `package`), and the existing temp-root coverage in `tests/scripts/link-game-assets.test.ts` still proves that behaviour; any opt-out used by tests is explicit, documented and defaults to composition ON.
- The three real-root consumers (`tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts`, `tests/electron/app-icon-build-output.test.ts`, `tests/vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts`) each run to completion repeatedly under concurrent load with no `ENOENT`, at a single deterministic preset (they must not inherit a caller-dependent `GAMES_CONFIG` that changes what they compose).
- The transient retry-once signatures in `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` are **not** extended to accept this `ENOENT` — the race is fixed, not masked.
- A regression test asserts the isolation contract (real-root test builds do not write to `public/assets`), and the Vite contract assertions of both electron build tests still hold (relative `./assets/...` for electron, `/Tableau-Card-Engine/` for production, icon/manifest copies present).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/DEVELOPER.md` → game-asset composition / test profiles, `AGENTS.md` if a test profile or runner flag changes, and the plugin's header comment).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A red unit run means the change is broken again rather than that two test files happened to build at the same moment, so agents and producers no longer burn cycles re-running or waiving an unrelated flake.

## Constraints

- Composition behaviour for real dev/build/package runs must not change: switching presets (e.g. `full` → `core-only`) must still clean stale links, and dangling links must still be pruned before Vite copies the public dir (`CG-0MWTSRRWU0062OMI`).
- Worktree-aware sibling resolution (`CG-0MWTVP7AI008RAPB`) must keep working: a worktree build still resolves `../tce-<game>` against the main checkout.
- Do not weaken the electron/Pages base-path and app-icon assertions — they are the reason these builds exist; if a build must run against a snapshot `publicDir`, the assertions must still see the real copied icon/manifest files.
- Do not use retry/tolerance to hide the failure; no `sleep`-based synchronisation in test code.
- Any change to test profiles, npm scripts or the runner is a workflow change → same-commit doc update per the project doc-update policy.

## Existing state

- `scripts/vite-game-assets-plugin.ts` runs `composeGameAssets` in `configResolved` and again in `buildStart`; it is registered unconditionally in `vite.config.ts` with `projectRoot` = Vite's resolved `root` (the real checkout or worktree).
- `scripts/link-game-assets.ts` composition is **destructive by design**: it creates/replaces links for the selected preset, removes links for games the preset no longer selects, and prunes dangling links. It is idempotent but not side-effect free, and it is driven per-process by `GAMES_CONFIG`.
- Real-root builders in the `unit` project (`include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']`, `maxWorkers: 4`, file parallelism on):
  - `tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts` — 2 builds, sets `GAMES_CONFIG=core-only` and restores it.
  - `tests/electron/app-icon-build-output.test.ts` — 3 builds, same `core-only` pin.
  - `tests/vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts` — `createServer()` with the real config and **no** preset pin, so it inherits the ambient preset (`full` under `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` and the typed `/skill:test` profiles).
- Vite 6.4.1 `copyDir` (`node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-D4NMHUTW.js:6859`) walks the live tree with `readdirSync` + `statSync` per entry; `prepareOutDir` calls it before the rollup `buildStart`, so the plugin's `buildStart` re-sync cannot cause (or heal) this particular window.
- The earlier, different variant of this signature (`public/assets/cards/lost-cities/…` dangling in an audit worktree, `CG-0MWTOUXMY004F5N8`) was waived as an execution-environment artefact and mitigated by dangling-link pruning (`CG-0MWTSRRWU0062OMI`). Pruning cannot fix this variant: the link is *valid* at scan time and is removed by a concurrent composition.
- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` classifies retryable transients by signature (worker RPC timeout, browser WebSocket drop, dynamic-import fetch failure); an `ENOENT` from the public-dir copy is not one, so the run is reported red.

## Desired change

Stop automated builds from sharing a mutable composed-asset tree. Concretely (mechanism open, options below):

1. Give `gameAssetsPlugin` an explicit, documented composition switch so a test/config can run a real-root build without composing (composition stays ON by default for every real dev/build/package invocation), and wire it for Vitest contexts.
2. Make every real-root build/dev-server test deterministic about what it needs: pin a single preset for the whole unit suite (rather than per-file restore of an ambient `full`), and, where a test asserts copied public files, build against a per-worker snapshot of `public/` (`root`/`publicDir` override) so the contract is asserted against a tree no other worker can mutate.
3. Add the deterministic regression test (real-root build leaves `public/assets` unchanged) and keep the temp-fixture coverage that proves composition still works.

Options considered (recommendation first):

- **A — Isolate test builds (recommended).** Compose nothing from a test build, and give the electron build tests a private `public/` snapshot. Rationale: removes the shared-mutable-state race at its source, keeps the unit suite in one project with no cross-worker locking, and leaves production behaviour untouched. Cost: one small snapshot copy per real-root build test.
- **B — Serialise.** Acquire a cross-process advisory lock around *the whole* real-root `build()`/`createServer()` (not just composition) and retry when busy. Rationale: minimal code movement, but leaves a shared mutable tree, adds waiting/timeouts inside the unit suite, and a lock that is stale after a crash becomes a new flake class.
- **C — Split the project.** Move the three real-root files into a `build-contract` project with `fileParallelism: false` and run it as its own stage. Rationale: real isolation and no per-build copies, but it changes test profiles/CI and does not by itself stop a developer's concurrent `npm run dev` from composing into the same tree.

Recommendation is A, optionally combined with the preset pin in (2). If the implementer finds A's snapshot too costly for `public/`'s size, C is the documented fallback; B is the least preferred.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/vite-game-assets-plugin.ts` — needs the explicit composition switch (documented in the header comment) and to keep `configResolved`/`buildStart` semantics for real runs.
- `scripts/link-game-assets.ts` — unchanged composition semantics expected; confirm no signature change is needed for an opt-out path.
- `vite.config.ts` — wire the switch for Vitest contexts (and any snapshot `publicDir`/root plumbing the tests need).
- `tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts` — stop depending on mutating the real `public/assets`; keep both base-path assertions.
- `tests/electron/app-icon-build-output.test.ts` — same for the three builds; keep icon/manifest copy assertions.
- `tests/vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts` — pin its preset / opt out of composition so it cannot compose `full` links during a unit run.
- `tests/scripts/link-game-assets.test.ts` — home for the deterministic "real-root build leaves `public/assets` unchanged" regression test (temp fixtures already exist here).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — game-asset composition section (and test-profile section if the preset pin or a new flag is introduced).
- `AGENTS.md` — only if a test profile, runner flag or npm script changes.

## Related work

- `CG-0MWTSRRWU0062OMI` (completed) — composed-asset symlink composition is worktree-fragile; added dangling-link pruning. Same code path, different failure (dangling vs concurrently-removed).
- `CG-0MWTVP7AI008RAPB` (completed) — worktree-aware sibling resolution for `planGameAssetLinks`/`discoverGames`; must not regress.
- `CG-0MWTOUXMY004F5N8` (completed, waived) — the earlier `ENOENT` from a *dangling* composed link during an audit-exec worktree full-suite run; fixed by pruning, not by isolation.
- `CG-0MWUOF1RA008OKSI` (completed) — the run in which this flake was observed (1 failed / 293 files, green on re-run).
- `CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N` / `CG-0MUFH228N000NRIF` — precedent items where cross-worker contention in a shared suite produced false-red runs; same "fix the isolation, do not add tolerance" principle.
- Docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (§ game-asset composition, § testing / skill-integrated test profiles), `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`, `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the ambient preset under the runners is `full` while the electron build tests pin `core-only`; both create and remove links in the same tree. Evidence: `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh:89` exports `GAMES_CONFIG="${GAMES_CONFIG:-full}"`, the electron tests set `core-only`, and `tests/vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts` pins nothing. A wrong assumption here only changes *which* mutator is involved, not the fix shape.
- **Assumption:** no test legitimately depends on `public/assets/games/*` being composed in the unit project (they are sibling-game assets; game suites run in their own repos). To be re-checked during implementation; if one does, it must opt in explicitly rather than rely on ambient composition.
- **Risk — coverage loss:** disabling composition under Vitest could hide a composition regression. Mitigation: composition stays covered by the temp-root suite in `tests/scripts/link-game-assets.test.ts`, and real `npm run build` remains unchanged.
- **Risk — snapshot cost/staleness:** a per-worker `public/` copy could be large or diverge from the real tree mid-run. Mitigation: prefer `fs.cpSync` with symlink dereference off where possible, snapshot immediately before `build()`, and keep icon/base-path assertions asserting what Vite actually emitted.
- **Risk — workflow churn:** if option C is chosen, test profiles, CI stages and docs all move. Mitigation: doc update in the same commit (project doc-update policy) and a re-check of the typed `/skill:test` extension mapping.
- **Risk — scope creep:** while here it is tempting to rework composition into a content-addressed, read-only overlay for all builds. Out of scope: record any such idea as a separate linked work item rather than widening this fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is this the same failure as the previously waived `vite-base-gating` `ENOENT` (`CG-0MWTOUXMY004F5N8`)?" — Answer (agent, research): "No. That variant was a *dangling* link (target missing inside an audit-exec worktree) and was mitigated by pruning (`CG-0MWTSRRWU0062OMI`). This variant fails on a link whose target exists: `copyDir` `readdir`s `public/assets/games`, a concurrent composition unlinks `games/main-street`, and the following `statSync` throws. Pruning cannot see it." Research: `scripts/link-game-assets.ts` (`pruneDanglingComposedLinks` uses `existsSync` and would classify the link healthy), Vite 6.4.1 `copyDir`/`prepareOutDir` in `dep-D4NMHUTW.js:6859`/`46291`, and `CG-0MWTOUXMY004F5N8`'s waiver comment.
- Q: "Which processes can mutate the shared tree during a unit run?" — Answer (agent, research): "Any build or dev-server start using the real `vite.config.ts`: `tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts` (2 builds, `core-only`), `tests/electron/app-icon-build-output.test.ts` (3 builds, `core-only`), and `tests/vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts` (`createServer`, ambient preset = `full` under the runners). A developer's concurrent `npm run dev` is the same class of mutator outside CI." Research: `rg "build\(\{|createServer\(" tests` plus the per-file `GAMES_CONFIG` handling, `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh:89`.
- Q: "Should the retry-once runner accept this signature so a flake never turns a gate red?" — Answer (agent, assumption): "No. The gate must report a genuine race; masking it would hide a real, fixed-able defect and contradict the runner's documented policy (`scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` deliberately keeps acceptance narrow)." Recorded as a constraint/AC rather than an open question.
- Q: "Which fix shape should be preferred (isolate / serialise / split project)?" — Answer (agent, assumption, routine): "Isolate test builds (option A), with the existing temp-root tests keeping composition covered. This is an implementation choice, cheap to reverse, and does not change any outward-facing contract; option C is documented as the fallback if the snapshot proves too costly." **Recommended:** A — isolation removes the shared mutable state that causes the race; serialising (B) leaves it in place and adds a new stale-lock flake class.

### Related work items

## Summary

A deterministic regression test proving that a Vite `build()` (and `createServer()`) on the **real project root** never mutates `public/assets`. The composed-link set is read before and after the build and must be identical.

This is the **reproduction**: on today's behaviour a `GAMES_CONFIG=core-only` build removes composed links (e.g. `public/assets/games/main-street`) because `gameAssetsPlugin` composes during `configResolved`/`buildStart`. The test is written first (red) and goes green once the composition opt-out is wired for Vitest contexts.

## Context

Parent `CG-0MWW6BWZB00968NQ`: `tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts` intermittently fails with `ENOENT` because Vite 6.4.1 `copyDir` (`readdirSync` then `statSync`) walks the shared `public/assets` tree while another worker's composition unlinks a link. Pruning cannot help — the link is valid at scan time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test in the `unit` project asserts before/after equality of the composed-link set under `public/assets/games/` (relative path + link target for each symlink, sorted).
- The baseline is established deterministically **inside the test** (a direct `composeGameAssets()` call with a fixed preset, e.g. `full`), so the assertion cannot pass trivially on an already-empty tree left by an earlier `core-only` run.
- In a checkout with no sibling game games present (`composeGameAssets` reports every selected game as `missingGames`), the test skips the mutation assertion with an explicit, printed skip reason instead of passing vacuously — the skip must name why (no siblings) so a silently weakened test is visible.
- The test fails deterministically against current behaviour (composition ON for a real-root build removes/creates links).
- The test passes once composition is disabled for Vitest-context builds.
- The test is deterministic: no sleeps, no polling, no retries, no tolerance windows.
- The test cleans up its temp `outDir` on both success and failure.
- Existing temp-fixture composition coverage in the same file is unchanged and still passes.

- Parent AC traceability (ac1): Unit-suite (and other automated) builds of the real project root never mutate `public/assets` — a `build()`/`createServer()` run leaves the composed-link set unchanged, pinned by a deterministic test that asserts before/after link-set equality for a real-root build (this is the reproduction: it fails on today's behaviour, where a `core-only` build removes `games/main-street`).
- Parent AC traceability (ac5): A regression test asserts the isolation contract (real-root test builds do not write to `public/assets`), and the Vite contract assertions of both electron build tests still hold (relative `./assets/...` for electron, `/Tableau-Card-Engine/` for production, icon/manifest copies present).


## Implementation

1. Add a helper that reads the composed-link set: for each entry under `public/assets/games/`, record `{ relativePath, target }` where `target` is `fs.readlinkSync` for symlinks and a sentinel for real directories/files; sort by path.
2. Add a test case: capture the set, run `build({ mode: 'development', root: REPO_ROOT, configFile: real vite.config.ts, build: { outDir: temp, emptyOutDir: true } })`, capture again, assert deep equality.
3. Wrap in `try/finally` so the temp `outDir` is always removed.
4. Assert (in a comment or an adjacent assertion) that the test is the documented reproduction of `CG-0MWW6BWZB00968NQ`.

## Definition of done

- `npx vitest run --project unit tests/scripts/link-game-assets.test.ts` shows the new case red before the opt-out lands and green afterwards.
- No source-grep assertions — the test asserts observable filesystem state.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/scripts/link-game-assets.test.ts` — home for the new case (existing temp-fixture tests live here).
- `scripts/vite-game-assets-plugin.ts` — the composition entry point under test (no edit in this child).

## Impact

A red unit run means a real problem again rather than two test files happening to build at the same moment, so agents and producers stop burning cycles re-running or waiving an unrelated flake.

data.description:
## Summary

Make the three real-root build/dev-server tests deterministic and independent of the shared `public/` tree: pin a single preset for the whole unit suite, and give the electron build tests a per-worker snapshot of `public/` so their icon/manifest assertions read a tree no other worker can mutate.

## Context

Parent `CG-0MWW6BWZB00968NQ`. Real-root consumers in the `unit` project:

- `tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts` — 2 builds, sets `GAMES_CONFIG=core-only` then restores an ambient value.
- `tests/electron/app-icon-build-output.test.ts` — 3 builds, same pin/restore.
- `tests/vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts` — `createServer()` with the real config and **no** preset pin, so it inherits `full` under the runners.

Once composition is off under Vitest, the remaining exposure is (a) tests inheriting a caller-dependent `GAMES_CONFIG`, and (b) tests asserting copied public files from a tree a concurrent `npm run dev` (or another process) can still change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All three files run under a **single deterministic preset** that does not depend on the caller's `GAMES_CONFIG`; none restores an ambient value that could differ mid-run.
- `tests/vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts` no longer inherits an ambient preset (pin explicitly).
- The electron build tests build against a **per-worker snapshot** of `public/` (temp dir populated from the repo `public/` with symlinks dereferenced or links copied faithfully) used as `publicDir`, so icon/manifest assertions read an immutable tree.
- The base-path assertions are unchanged and still hold: `./assets/...` for electron, `/Tableau-Card-Engine/` for production, no absolute `/assets/` in electron output.
- Icon/manifest assertions still assert files Vite actually emitted (favicon.svg, apple-touch-icon.png, icon-192.png, icon-512.png, site.webmanifest, `404.html`) from the snapshot.
- No `sleep`-based synchronisation, no retry loops, no tolerance windows in any of the three files.
- Each file passes repeatedly and concurrently (e.g. three concurrent runs of the `unit` project) with no `ENOENT`.
- Snapshot cleanup is guaranteed in `finally` blocks; no temp dirs leak.

- Parent AC traceability (ac3): The three real-root consumers (`tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts`, `tests/electron/app-icon-build-output.test.ts`, `tests/vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts`) each run to completion repeatedly under concurrent load with no `ENOENT`, at a single deterministic preset (they must not inherit a caller-dependent `GAMES_CONFIG` that changes what they compose).


## Implementation

1. Add a small shared test helper (e.g. `tests/helpers/public-snapshot.ts`) that copies the repo `public/` into a `mkdtemp` dir once per file (or per build where a fresh copy is required), returning `{ publicDir, cleanup }`. Copy with `fs.cpSync({ recursive: true, verbatimSymlinks: false })` so composed links resolve to real content, or skip `assets/games` entirely — decide from size (measure first).
2. Thread `publicDir` through the `build()`/`createServer()` calls in the electron tests.
3. Pin `GAMES_CONFIG` explicitly in all three files (e.g. a `beforeAll` that saves, sets `core-only`/a fixed preset, `afterAll` that restores), with a comment explaining why the pin is suite-wide and not per-file-ambient.
4. Measure and record the snapshot cost in the child's completion comment (size + wall clock); if it proves prohibitive, stop and escalate on the parent before choosing option C.

## Definition of done

- Unit project green repeatedly; no `ENOENT` under concurrent load.
- Snapshot cost documented (size, per-run wall clock) with the mitigation decision recorded.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts`
- `tests/electron/app-icon-build-output.test.ts`
- `tests/vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts`
- `tests/helpers/public-snapshot.ts` (new)
- `vite.config.ts` (only if the preset pin needs config-level support)

## Impact

Unit-suite runs stop failing with spurious `ENOENT` errors when a build, dev server or another worker is touching `public/`, so a green run means the suite is actually green.

## Summary

Document the composition switch and the test-isolation contract, then prove the whole change with the unit gate and (before any push) the full suite.

## Impact

A red unit run means the change under test is broken again — concurrent test builds no longer corrupt the shared composed-asset tree, so agents and producers stop burning cycles re-running or waiving an unrelated `ENOENT` flake.

## Context

Parent `CG-0MWW6BWZB00968NQ`. Any change to test profiles, npm scripts or the runner is a workflow change under the project doc-update policy (`AGENTS.md` → Doc-Update Policy), so docs land in the same change set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` game-asset composition section documents: composition is ON by default; Vitest-context builds run with composition off; real-root tests use a private `public/` snapshot; and the reason (shared mutable tree + Vite's `readdirSync`/`statSync` copy window), referencing `CG-0MWW6BWZB00968NQ`.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` testing section notes the single deterministic preset used by the real-root build tests (no caller-dependent `GAMES_CONFIG`).
- `README.md` updated where it describes building/running (verify whether it mentions composition; if it does, note the Vitest opt-out; if not, record the check in the completion comment).
- `AGENTS.md` updated **only if** a test profile, runner flag or npm script changed; if nothing changed there, the completion comment records why `AGENTS.md` was deliberately left alone.
- `scripts/vite-game-assets-plugin.ts` header comment describes the switch and the default (delivered by the opt-out child; verify here).
- No doc claims behaviour the code does not have (e.g. do not claim `npm run build` is isolated).
- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` is **unchanged** — the `ENOENT` signature is not added to the retryable transients; record this explicitly in the completion comment.
- Unit gate green (`/skill:test --type unit`), then the full suite green at the final commit before any push to `dev`.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes — the complete suite is run via the test skill at the final commit and is green.

- Parent AC traceability (ac4): The transient retry-once signatures in `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` are **not** extended to accept this `ENOENT` — the race is fixed, not masked.
- Parent AC traceability (ac6): All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/DEVELOPER.md` → game-asset composition / test profiles, `AGENTS.md` if a test profile or runner flag changes, and the plugin's header comment).
- Parent AC traceability (ac7): Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.


## Implementation

1. Update `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (composition + testing sections).
2. Review `AGENTS.md`; update only if a profile/script/flag actually changed.
3. Confirm the plugin header comment covers the switch as documented.
4. Run the unit profile, then the full suite via the test skill at the final commit; record results in the completion comment.

## Definition of done

- Docs describe the shipped behaviour exactly; `/skill:test --type unit` green; full suite green at the commit under review (populating the audit cache).

**Key Files:**

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- `README.md` (conditional — verify)
- `AGENTS.md` (conditional)
- `scripts/vite-game-assets-plugin.ts` (comment verification only)
- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` (verification only — must be unchanged)
